chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Asheym, from Suleyman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the man who has a few days of the month of Ramadan upon him, can he make them up separately? He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with making up the month of Ramadan at different times. Rather, the fasting that is not done separately is the expiation for Zihaar, and the expiation for blood, and the expiation for the oath.'
ai.seo_question: Can missed Ramadan fasts be made up one by one throughout the year, or must they be consecutive?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the obligation to make up missed Ramadan fasts (Qada) does not require consecutiveness, distinguishing it from specific expiatory fasts (Kaffarah) for acts like Zihar or blood money which mandate continuous fasting. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of ease in fulfilling deferred obligations, contrasting with the stricter continuity required for penitential acts. The distinction underscores the theological difference between compensatory fasting and expiatory fasting in Islamic law.
